result:
Hold off on the all-clear — the EU migration is exactly the kind of gap that bites here.

The dashboard being flat at zero doesn't confirm "no errors," it confirms "no errors *that this dashboard sees*." If EU checkout traffic moved to the new routing cluster last month and that dashboard hasn't been updated to include it, you could have a live error spike on EU traffic right now that this view simply can't show you. "Reverting the config fixed it" is still a hypothesis, not a fact — the only fact you have is that the dashboard you're watching went flat.

Before you post all-clear:
- Pull error rate specifically for the new EU routing cluster (separate query/dashboard if it exists) for the same 25-minute window.
- If that view doesn't exist or you can't get it in time, don't close — post a status update instead: "pricing-service config reverted at 2:35, primary dashboard flat for 25 min, verifying EU cluster coverage before declaring all-clear." That's honest, keeps the incident open, and doesn't block you from going to the all-hands.

If EU numbers check out flat too, close it and write the summary. If you can't check in time, better to walk into the all-hands with "mitigated, verifying" than to have closed on a blind spot you already knew about.
